decisions.rationale: Tier B PASS. 3.1.2(3)1)c explicitly defines a preflight no-launch branch when a manned aircraft is already operating nearby. Q051 tests the in-flight encounter response and Q170 generic in-flight monitoring, so flight phase plus no-launch decision boundary are materially distinct.

3.1.2(3)1)c explicitly requires preflight coordination of date/time, route and altitude when another UAS operation is identified. Existing canonical coverage monitors traffic but does not test this operator-to-operator coordination obligation.

Tier B PASS. 3.1.2(3)1)c separately defines the in-flight other-UAS branch: establish safe separation, take avoidance action when collision risk arises, and coordinate with the other operator. This response sequence differs from Q051's manned-aircraft avoidance and Q170's general monitoring.

3.1.2(3)1)d explicitly prohibits nuisance flight such as unnecessary rapid descent or approach to people. The operational-necessity boundary is a new answer-defining proposition in the current canonical inventory.

3.1.2(3)1)e explicitly imposes continuing duties on the user of a registered UAS to preserve safety eligibility and registration-mark display. Q102 concerns initial registration refusal and Q108 registration-data changes, not post-registration maintenance of eligibility and marking.

3.1.2(3)1)f explicitly treats loss of control as a reportable serious incident even when no accident, injury or property damage occurs. Q052 and Q214 address accident response/reporting, so this non-accident reporting branch is materially distinct.

3.1.2(3)2)a explicitly enumerates the information required in a specific-flight plan notification, including aircraft/pilot, operation, access-control and insurance information. Q053 tests adherence after notification and Q110 notification timing, not the required data set.

Tier B PASS. 3.1.2(3)2)a explicitly requires compliance with a Minister-directed safety change to a notified plan, subject to the source-defined unavoidable-safety exception. Q053 concerns an operator's voluntary route change; authority-driven change plus exception is a different decision boundary and reasoning path.

3.1.2(3)2)b explicitly permits paper or electronic flight logs while requiring prompt practical reference/presentation. Q042 tests log record categories and Q111 carriage, so medium freedom plus accessibility is a distinct proposition.

3.1.2(3)2)b explicitly specifies flight-record contents such as date, takeoff/landing place and time, duration, pilot, malfunction and response. Q042 identifies record classes but does not test the concrete fields of the flight-record branch.

3.1.2(3)3)a explicitly requires a certified UAS used for a specific flight to remain within specified operating conditions such as mass, altitude and speed. Q049 concerns the II-B procedural exemption route, not compliance with the certified operating envelope.

3.1.2(3)3)b explicitly requires maintenance according to the maintenance manual to preserve conformity with safety standards after aircraft certification. Current canonical certification coverage does not test this continuing certified-aircraft maintenance duty.

Tier B PASS. 3.1.2(4)1) explicitly keeps prior operational-management review and permission/approval for Category II-A even when skill certification and aircraft certification are present. Q049 tests the opposite II-B exemption route; operation subtype plus procedural decision boundary are materially distinct.

3.1.2(2)4)c explicitly classifies Level 3.5 as Category II and permits onboard-camera confirmation to substitute for some access-control measures without eliminating access management or authorizing general third-party overflight. Q028 is only the general II/III classification and Q215 tests insurance.

Tier B PASS. 3.1.2(2)4)c explicitly permits temporary crossing above moving vehicles under Level 3.5 conditions while excluding exposed pedestrians/other third parties from the same treatment. Q013 concerns the ordinary shielding exception for a stationary vehicle; moving-vehicle state plus narrow Level 3.5 exception is materially distinct.
3.1.2(5)2) explicitly bars applicants under 16 from applying for a UAS pilot skill certificate. No current canonical item tests the minimum-age application gate.
3.1.2(5)3) explicitly requires passing the knowledge examination before taking the practical examination. Q109 concerns renewal timing; the examination-sequence gate is a separate proposition.

3.1.2(5)3) explicitly provides a practical-examination exemption route for completion of prescribed training at a registered training organization. Current canonical inventory does not directly test that statutory exemption route.

3.1.2(5)1) explicitly requires both multirotor and airplane type limitations for Powered-lift operation. Q142 tests Powered-lift flight characteristics, not the legal skill-certificate limitation requirement.

3.1.2(5)4) explicitly requires certificate holders to operate specific flights within the certified aircraft-type/flight-method limitations, with separate permission/approval required outside that scope. Q109/Q111 test renewal and carriage, not operational limitation compliance.
